newsitem.title: QATAR: Enron says hopes for Qatar LNG JV soon.
newsitem.headline: Enron says hopes for Qatar LNG JV soon.

text.p: Enron Corp said on Wednesday it hoped to seal a joint venture agreement with Qatar soon to set up a $5 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project.

"Enron holds a letter of intent with Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) to form a joint venture for the sale of LNG. Negotiations are going well and we hope to have an agreement finalised soon," said Enron spokeswoman Kelly Kimberly.
It is the first time the U.S. energy giant has publicly stated its determination to go ahead with a third LNG plant in Qatar, despite initial hiccups.
"Enron considers LNG a viable fuel source for its projects (especially those it is implementing in India)", Kimberly said in a written statement prepared for Reuters.

Enron signed the letter of intent with Qatar on January 18, 1995 to produce five million tonnes of LNG from 2001, with 2.5 million tonnes targeted at Israel and the remaining destined for one of its power projects in India.

But the project became embroiled in commercial rivalries and politics in Tel Aviv and Bombay, the capital of western Indian state of Maharashtra where the Dabhol power project promoted by Enron is located.
The company now appears to have weathered the storm, but other issues associated with the Qatari project and Enron's commitments to various customers still remain to be resolved.
One of them is its rival Mobil's concern the Enron project might cut into the markets of other similar Qatari projects.

During its dispute with the Maharashtra government over the Dabhol project, Enron signed a series of letters of intent with various energy agencies in India and the government-run Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL) to set up power projects or supply around five million tonnes of gas a year on a long-term basis.
This has increased pressure on Enron to seek immediate supply sources.

Enron has set itself a schedule to complete all formalities to sign a joint venture agreement with QGPC by the end of March, to organise finance by 1998 and start producing LNG in 2001, a local Enron official said.
